s: In which year did Muhammad Ali Jinnah join the All-India Muslim League?
x: Jinnah joined the Muslim League in 1913, although he was also associated with the Congress-League cooperation that culminated in the Lucknow Pact.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tilak Home Rule League – Annie Besant
Besant Home Rule League – Nawab Salimullah
x: Nawab Salimullah is linked with the 1906 Muslim League. The Tilak league was led by Tilak, the Besant league by Annie Besant, and the Lucknow Pact by Jinnah and Tilak.

s: The Simla Deputation of 1906 demanded which of the following for Muslims?
x: The deputation demanded separate electorates and weightage, citing the Muslims' contribution to the defence of the Empire.

s: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906?
x: Aga Khan III organised and led the Simla Deputation; Salimullah proposed the League.

s: In seeking weightage, the Simla Deputation cited the Muslims' contribution to:
x: The Deputation demanded separate electorates and weightage, citing the Muslims' contribution to the defence of the Empire.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Simla Deputation of 1906:
1. It was led by Aga Khan III.
2. It sought special safeguards for Muslims in government services.
3. It met Lord Curzon at Simla.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Deputation met Lord Minto, not Curzon, on 1 October 1906; statements 1 and 2 are correct.

s: Who proposed the formation of the All India Muslim League at Dacca in 1906?
x: Nawab Salimullah proposed the League on 30 December 1906; Aga Khan was its first president and Syed Ameer Ali set up the London branch.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Muslim League was formed in 1906 at Dhaka.
The Muslim League aimed to protect Muslim political interests.
The Muslim League was formed in 1907 at Karachi.
Nawab Salimullah was associated with the Muslim League.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Muslim League was formed in 1906 at Dhaka with Nawab Salimullah to protect Muslim political interests. Karachi in 1907 was its first annual session.

s: Which of the following was an aim of the All-India Muslim League in its early phase?
o: Launching an immediate armed revolt against British rule
Promoting loyalty to the British Empire
Opposing British rule through mass agitation
x: The early League aimed at loyalty to the British Empire, protection of Muslim interests and keeping Muslims away from the Congress; armed revolt was not an aim.

s: At the session of which body was the All India Muslim League founded at Dacca?
x: The League was founded on 30 December 1906 at the session of the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

s: Where was the headquarters of the All India Muslim League?
x: The League was founded at Dacca, but its headquarters was at Lucknow.

s: What stand did the early Muslim League take on the partition of Bengal?
x: The early League supported the partition of Bengal.

s: In which city was a branch of the All India Muslim League set up under Syed Ameer Ali in 1908?
x: The London branch of the Muslim League was set up in 1908 with Syed Ameer Ali as its president.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First annual session of the Muslim League – Karachi
Second session of the Muslim League – Lucknow
x: The League's first annual session was at Karachi. It was founded at Dhaka (1906), its second session was at Amritsar and the Lucknow Pact was signed at Lucknow.

s: Where was the second session of the Muslim League (1908) held?
x: The first annual session was at Karachi (1907) and the second at Amritsar (1908).

s: On which date did the Simla Deputation led by Aga Khan III meet Lord Minto?
x: The Simla Deputation, led by Aga Khan III, met Lord Minto on 1 October 1906.

s: On which date was the annulment of the partition of Bengal announced at the Delhi Durbar?
x: At the Delhi Durbar of 12 December 1911 the annulment was announced through King George V and the capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi.

s: At the Delhi Durbar of 12 December 1911, from where to where was the capital shifted?
x: The Delhi Durbar annulled the partition of Bengal and shifted the capital from Calcutta to Delhi.

s: Where was the All-India Muslim League founded on 30 December 1906?
x: It was founded at Dacca at the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

s: Who was the first (honorary) president of the All-India Muslim League?
x: Aga Khan III was its first honorary president; the proposal came from Nawab Salimullah.

s: Who proposed the formation of the All-India Muslim League at Dacca in December 1906?
x: The proposal came from Nawab Salimullah of Dacca; Aga Khan III was the first honorary president.

s: Which event of 1906 preceded the grant of separate electorates for Muslims by the Morley-Minto Reforms?
x: The Simla Deputation of 1906 asked for separate electorates, granted by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.

s: Who was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1909)?
x: S.P. Sinha was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1909), as Law Member.

s: Which post did John Morley hold at the time of the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
x: John Morley was the Secretary of State for India and Lord Minto was the Viceroy.

s: What kind of elections did the Indian Councils Act, 1909 provide for?
o: Held in a single national constituency
Not held; all non-officials were nominated
x: The 1909 reforms introduced indirect, multi-tier elections, not direct universal elections.

s: Up to how many additional members of the Central Legislative Council did the Indian Councils Act, 1909 allow?
x: Additional members were raised up to 60, but an official majority was kept at the Centre.

s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1909, members could discuss the budget. What could they NOT do?
x: Members could discuss the budget, ask supplementary questions and move resolutions, but could not vote on the budget.

s: What was the main aim of the Morley-Minto Reforms?
o: Rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty
Transfer the capital from Delhi to Calcutta
Abolish princely states and establish a republic
x: Morley and Minto sought to rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty through limited constitutional concessions and separate electorates.

s: In which capacity did S.P. Sinha join the Viceroy's Executive Council in 1909?
x: S.P. Sinha was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council, as Law Member.

s: Who called the Morley-Minto Reforms an incomplete deal between democracy and bureaucracy?
x: Ramsay MacDonald described the 1909 reforms as an incomplete deal between democracy and bureaucracy.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act, 1909:
1. An official majority was kept in the Central Legislative Council.
2. Provincial councils had a non-official majority.
3. Members could vote on the budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Members could discuss the budget but not vote on it; statements 1 and 2 are correct.

s: Lord Minto II succeeded which Viceroy in 1905?
x: Minto II replaced Curzon in 1905 and was Viceroy till 1910.

s: By which Act were separate electorates for Muslims introduced?
x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 enlarged the legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

s: What is the name of the provision that gave Muslims more seats than their population share in provinces where they were a minority?
x: The Lucknow Pact provided weightage to Muslims in minority provinces, giving them representation greater than their population share.

s: In which year were separate electorates for Muslims granted by reforms?
x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909, following the Simla Deputation (1906), gave Muslims separate electorates.

s: Who were the principal negotiators of the Lucknow Pact?
x: The Pact was negotiated by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Muhammad Ali Jinnah with the Muslim League's Young Party.

s: Who presided over the Lucknow Congress session of December 1916?
x: Ambika Charan Majumdar presided over the Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916.

s: The Congress-League alliance was forged at which Congress session?
x: The 1916 Lucknow session saw the Congress-League alliance (Lucknow Pact), the Moderate-Extremist reunion and Tilak's return.

s: Under the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted which major concession to the Muslim League?
o: Direct British appointment of Muslim representatives
x: The Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims, which was a major concession under the Lucknow Pact.

s: Under the Lucknow Pact, a bill affecting a community could not pass if opposed by ____ of that community's members.
x: The communal veto barred a bill if three-fourths of the affected community's members opposed it.

s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 accepted which of the following as the common goal?
x: The Pact accepted self-government as its goal, with separation of executive and judiciary and elected majorities in provincial legislatures.

s: At Lucknow in 1916 the Extremists re-entered the Congress after how many years?
x: The Extremists had been out since Surat 1907, so they returned after 9 years.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Lucknow Pact, 1916:
1. It called for the separation of the executive and the judiciary.
2. It called for elected majorities in provincial legislatures.
3. After it, the Congress and the League stopped holding separate annual sessions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The two bodies still held separate annual sessions, a limit of the Pact; statements 1 and 2 are correct.

s: Who presided over the Muslim League session held at Lucknow in 1916?
x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah presided over the Muslim League session at Lucknow in 1916.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Lucknow Pact
2. Formation of the Muslim League
3. Jallianwala Bagh massacre
4. Morley-Minto Reforms
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Muslim League 1906, Morley-Minto Reforms 1909, Lucknow Pact 1916, Jallianwala Bagh 1919.

s: At which INC session did the Moderates and Extremists reunite?
x: The Extremists re-entered the Congress at Lucknow in 1916, the year of the Lucknow Pact.

s: Who is associated with the description 'Father of the Communal Electorate'?
x: Lord Minto is associated with the title 'Father of the Communal Electorate' because the Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

s: The Government of India Act, 1919 extended communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and which other group?
x: The 1919 Act extended communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans; depressed classes, women and labour got it in 1935.

s: Which Act extended separate electorates to the depressed classes, women and labour?
x: The 1935 Act gave provincial autonomy and extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the significance of 1909 and 1916 is correct?
o: 1909 marked the legal beginning of separate electorates, while 1916 marked the high point of Congress-League unity.
1909 marked the establishment of provincial autonomy, while 1916 marked the end of communal politics.
1909 marked the end of separate electorates, while 1916 marked the beginning of the Muslim League.
Both 1909 and 1916 marked phases of complete constitutional separation between Congress and the League.
x: The year 1909 is associated with the legal start of separate electorates, whereas 1916 is regarded as the high point of Congress-League unity.

s: The 'Father of the Communal Electorate' held which office?
o: Law Member of the Executive Council
x: Lord Minto, the Father of the Communal Electorate, was Viceroy (1905-1910); Morley was Secretary of State.

s: Lord Minto used separate electorates for Muslims mainly to:
x: Minto used separate electorates to turn Muslims against the Congress; they divided the electorate on religious lines.

s: Which Act provided for an All-India Federation?
x: The 1935 Act prescribed an All-India Federation; the 1919 Act introduced provincial dyarchy and bicameralism at the Centre.

s: Which Act gave the right to discuss the budget and brought indirect election of members?
x: The 1892 Act brought budget discussion and indirect election; 1909 brought separate Muslim electorates, 1919 dyarchy and 1935 provincial autonomy.

s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the 1909 and 1919 reforms?
o: The 1919 reforms abolished communal representation introduced in 1909.
The 1909 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates.
The 1909 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
Both reforms introduced provincial autonomy in the provinces.
x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims, while the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.

s: Under Provincial Dyarchy (1919), into which categories were subjects divided?
x: Provincial Dyarchy under the 1919 Act split subjects into reserved and transferred; the 1935 Act abolished it.

s: In which year were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted?
x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms are the Government of India Act, 1919, not 1929.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Indian Councils Act, 1892 – First indirect elections
Indian Councils Act, 1909 – Dyarchy at the Centre
x: Dyarchy at the Centre came with the 1935 Act; the 1909 Act introduced separate Muslim electorates.

s: Which Act introduced dyarchy at the Centre?
x: The 1935 Act abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced it at the Centre.

s: Which Act introduced bicameralism and direct elections at the Centre?
x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Act of 1919 brought provincial dyarchy and a bicameral central legislature with direct elections.

s: Who founded Yugantar (1906)?
x: Barindra Kumar Ghosh founded Yugantar (1906); P. Mitra founded Anushilan Samiti and Savarkar Abhinav Bharat.

s: Who planned the Barrah Dacoity of 1908 in Dhaka district?
x: Pulin Behari Das, leader of the Dhaka Anushilan Samiti and founder of the National School, Dhaka, planned the Barrah Dacoity.

s: Barindra Kumar Ghosh, founder of Yugantar, was the younger brother of whom?
x: Barindra Kumar Ghosh was the younger brother of Aurobindo Ghosh; both were accused in the Alipore case.

s: The Indo-German, or Zimmerman, plot of 1915–17 was associated with which plan?
o: A plan to support the Simon Commission
A plan by Bagha Jatin to organise a revolt with German arms
A plan to establish a constitutional government through the Morley-Minto reforms
A plan to conduct the Chittagong Armoury Raid
x: The Indo-German plot involved Bagha Jatin’s plan to organise an armed revolt with German arms. He died in a gunfight at Balasore in 1915.

s: Where did Bagha Jatin die in a gunfight in 1915?
x: Bagha Jatin, leader of the Indo-German plan, died in a gunfight at Balasore in 1915.

s: Who founded the Mitra Mela in 1899, which later became associated with Abhinav Bharat?
x: V.D. Savarkar founded Mitra Mela in 1899. It later developed into the revolutionary organisation Abhinav Bharat.

s: Who among the following was associated with founding the Hindustan Republican Association?
x: Sachindranath Sanyal, Jogesh Chatterjee and Ram Prasad Bismil were associated with founding the HRA.

s: After which of the following was Abhinav Bharat named?
x: Abhinav Bharat (Young India Society) was named after Mazzini's Young Italy.

s: V.D. Savarkar was associated with which of the following?
x: V.D. Savarkar founded Abhinav Bharat in 1904. The HRA, HSRA and Assembly bombing belong to other revolutionaries.

s: Who assassinated A.M.T. Jackson, Collector of Nasik?
x: Anant Kanhere killed Jackson, which led to Savarkar's implication in the Nasik Conspiracy Case and his sentence in the Andamans.

s: V.D. Savarkar was arrested in London in 1910. At which place did his attempted escape fail?
x: Savarkar’s attempted escape failed at Marseilles in 1910.

s: In which year was Savarkar's 'Hindutva' published?
x: Hindutva appeared in 1923; The Indian War of Independence, 1857 in 1909.

s: In which case was V.D. Savarkar sentenced to life in the Andamans?
x: Savarkar got life in the Cellular Jail, Andamans, in the Nasik case.

s: Who wrote 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857'?
x: Savarkar wrote The Indian War of Independence, 1857 (1909) and Hindutva; Mukti Kon Pathe was Barindra Ghosh's.

s: Vasudev Balwant Phadke turned which community into a combat force in 1879?
x: Phadke's Ramosi Krishak Jatha (1879) turned the Ramoshi tribes into a combat force.

s: Who was the intended target in the Muzaffarpur Bomb Case?
x: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki targeted Magistrate Douglas Kingsford at Muzaffarpur.

s: Who was hanged for the Muzaffarpur bomb attack (1908)?
x: The bomb killed two British women instead of Kingsford; Khudiram Bose was hanged, while Prafulla Chaki shot himself.

s: Where did Vanchi Aiyar shoot Robert Ashe, Collector of Tirunelveli, in 1911?
x: Vanchi Aiyar shot Ashe at Maniyachi on 17 June 1911 and then shot himself.

s: Whom did the Chapekar brothers shoot in June 1897?
x: Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar shot Rand (and Lt Ayerst) at Poona against plague-control excesses.

s: Against what was the Chapekar brothers' attack at Poona (1897) a protest?
x: Their shooting of Rand was a protest against the excesses of plague-control measures.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Muzaffarpur bomb case (1908)?
o: Prafulla Chaki was hanged along with Khudiram
The bomb killed two British women
x: Prafulla Chaki shot himself before arrest; Khudiram alone was hanged, on 11 August 1908.

s: With whose Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation was Vanchi Aiyar's action of 1911 linked?
x: Vanchi Aiyar was linked to the Bharata Matha Association and V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation.

s: With which association was Vanchi Aiyar, who shot Collector Ashe in 1911, linked?
x: Vanchi Aiyar was linked to the Bharata Matha Association and to V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Assassination of W.C. Rand (1897) – Chapekar brothers
x: Phadke's Ramosi force (1879) was an earlier root, organised before the Chapekars shot Rand at Poona in 1897, not in 1909.

s: The approver Narendranath Goswami was shot inside Alipore jail by Kanailal Dutta and:
x: Goswami was shot inside Alipore jail by Kanailal Dutta and Satyendranath Bose, not abroad by Dhingra.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Alipore Bomb Case is correct?
o: It involved a raid on the Maniktala bomb factory, and Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted.
It was related to the killing of Curzon Wyllie in London.
It concerned the Kakori train action, and C.R. Das was the chief accused.
It was conducted in Nasik, and Barindra Ghosh was acquitted.
x: The Alipore Bomb Case followed the raid on the Maniktala bomb factory. Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted, while Barindra Ghosh received a life sentence; C.R. Das defended Aurobindo.

s: How many persons were accused in the Alipore Bomb Case?
x: 49 were accused, including Aurobindo and Barindra Ghosh; 19 were sentenced.

s: What sentence did Barindra Kumar Ghosh receive in the Alipore Bomb Case?
x: Barindra got life (Andaman Cellular Jail), while Aurobindo was acquitted.

s: Where was the bomb factory whose raid triggered the Alipore Bomb Case?
x: The Maniktala bomb factory in Calcutta was raided after Muzaffarpur, leading to the Alipore case.

s: Where in Delhi was the bomb thrown at Lord Hardinge's procession in 1912?
x: The bomb was thrown during Hardinge's state entry procession through Chandni Chowk; he was injured but not killed.

s: Which one of the following persons escaped after the Delhi Conspiracy Case by disguising himself and later went to Japan?
x: Rash Behari Bose escaped in disguise after the case and later went to Japan.

s: Who threw the bomb at Lord Hardinge in Delhi in 1912?
x: Basanta Kumar Biswas threw the bomb; Rash Behari Bose led the plan and escaped.

s: What happened to Lord Hardinge in the bomb attack of 23 December 1912?
o: He was not in the procession
x: Hardinge was injured, not killed, during his state entry into Delhi.

s: With whom is the Howrah (Howrah-Sibpur) Conspiracy Case of 1910 associated?
x: The Howrah Conspiracy Case (1910) is associated with Bagha Jatin.

s: In which year did the bomb attack on Lord Hardinge take place?
x: The Hardinge attack was in 1912, after Rand's killing (1897), Muzaffarpur (1908) and the Nasik case (1909).

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Assassination of Curzon Wyllie
2. Execution of Khudiram Bose
3. Bomb attack on Lord Hardinge
4. Killing of W.C. Rand
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Rand was killed in 1897, Khudiram was executed in 1908, Curzon Wyllie was shot in 1909 and the Hardinge bomb was in 1912.

s: What was a key limitation of the first phase of revolutionary nationalism?
o: Did not develop into a mass movement
x: It did not become a mass movement, and its Hindu-revivalist symbolism, such as Bhavani worship, restricted Muslim participation.

s: Who wrote the pamphlet 'Bhawani Mandir' (1905)?
x: Aurobindo wrote Bhawani Mandir (1905); Bhavani worship was a Hindu-revivalist symbol of the revolutionaries.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Bharat Mata Society was founded by Ajit Singh with Lala Lajpat Rai in Punjab, not in Bengal in 1906.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Dhaka Anushilan Samiti – Pulin Behari Das
Bharat Mata Society – Ajit Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai
Bharat Mata Society – Pulin Behari Das
x: The Bharat Mata Society was associated with Ajit Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai; Pulin Behari Das led the Dhaka branch of Anushilan Samiti.

s: In which region was the Bharat Mata Society of Ajit Singh active?
x: The Bharat Mata Society was a Punjab body of Ajit Singh with Lajpat Rai, not a Bengal one.

s: With whom is the revolutionary manual 'Mukti Kon Pathe' (1906) associated?
x: Mukti Kon Pathe (1906) was Barindra Kumar Ghosh's manual.

s: Who founded the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888 to oppose the Congress?
o: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan and Raja Shiv Prasad
x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan and Raja Shiv Prasad formed the United Indian Patriotic Association (1888) against the Congress.

s: Who started the Calcutta paper 'Sandhya'?
x: Sandhya, a paper backing revolutionary action, was run by Brahma Bandhab Upadhyay.

s: With whom was the United India House at Seattle associated?
o: Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
x: United India House, Seattle, was run by Taraknath Das and G.D. Kumar.

s: The word ‘Ghadar’ denotes which of the following?
x: ‘Ghadar’ means mutiny or rebellion, reflecting the revolutionary character of the organisation.

s: The members of the Ghadar Party were predominantly drawn from which group?
o: Punjabi Sikh immigrants in North America
x: The Ghadar Party drew most of its members from Punjabi Sikh immigrants living in North America.

s: Which one of the following was actively associated with the Ghadar rising?
x: Rash Behari Bose was actively associated with the Ghadar rising (UPSC 2022). Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee were not, and Bipin Chandra Pal was associated with the Calcutta Bande Mataram, not the Ghadar.

s: What was the planned date of the Ghadar uprising in the British Indian Army?
x: The pan-India revolt was planned for 21 February 1915, but informers betrayed the plan and it was crushed.

s: Kartar Singh Sarabha, executed on 16 November 1915 at the age of 19, was sentenced in which case?
x: Sarabha was executed in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case (with Vishnu Ganesh Pingle) after the failed Ghadar rising. The Delhi case (1912) concerned the Hardinge bomb, Kakori (1925) the HRA train action and Alipore (1908) the Maniktala bomb factory.

s: The Ghadar Party grew out of which organisation in San Francisco?
x: The Ghadar Party grew out of the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association, San Francisco.

s: How many Ghadar leaders were hanged under the Defence of India Act after the failed 1915 revolt?
x: After the planned February 1915 revolt was betrayed, 45 leaders were hanged under the Defence of India Act.

s: Sohan Singh Bhakna called which Ghadarite his 'General'?
x: Sohan Singh Bhakna, the first president, called Kartar Singh Sarabha his 'General'.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ghadar Party:
1. It was founded on 21 April 1913.
2. Its first meeting was held in Oregon.
3. Its headquarters was at Vancouver.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The party was founded on 21 April 1913 with its first meeting in Oregon. Its headquarters was Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco, not Vancouver.

s: In which year was Lala Har Dayal arrested in the USA after founding the Ghadar Party?
x: Har Dayal founded the Ghadar Party in 1913 and was arrested in the USA in 1914.

s:
Consider the following statements about Lala Har Dayal:
1. He belonged to the India House circle in London.
2. He was the first president of the Ghadar Party.
3. He was arrested in the USA in 1914.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Har Dayal was part of London's India House circle and was arrested in the USA in 1914. He was the Ghadar Party's secretary and moving spirit; its first president was Sohan Singh Bhakna.

s: What was the headquarters of the Ghadar Party at San Francisco called?
x: The Ghadar Party's headquarters was Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco; India House was Shyamji Krishna Varma's in London.

s: In which year was the Defence of India Act enacted?
x: The Defence of India Act came in 1915; the 1907 deportation was under Regulation III of 1818.

s: Where was the Ghadar revolt fixed for 21 February 1915 planned?
x: The Ghadar revolt was fixed for 21 February 1915 in Punjab but was betrayed.

s: Which unit rose in the Singapore Mutiny of February 1915?
x: Indian troops of the 5th Light Infantry rose under Ghadar influence.

s: Who among the following was associated with India House along with V.D. Savarkar and Lala Hardayal?
x: Madan Lal Dhingra was associated with India House along with Savarkar and Hardayal. Dhingra killed Curzon Wyllie in 1909.

s: From which city did Madame Bhikaji Cama bring out Bande Mataram?
x: Madame Bhikaji Cama brought out *Bande Mataram* from Paris and was associated with the Paris Indian Society.

s: Who founded the Paris Indian Society (1905)?
x: Madame Bhikaji Cama founded the Paris Indian Society in 1905; it was separate from Krishnavarma's India House.

s: Madame Bhikaji Cama came from which community?
x: Bhikaji Cama came from a rich Parsi family.

s: At which event did Madame Bhikaji Cama hoist the Indian national flag in 1907?
o: Indian National Congress session at Surat
Congress of Oppressed Nationalities at Brussels
x: On 22 August 1907 Bhikaji Cama hoisted the first Indian national flag at the International Socialist Congress, Stuttgart.

s: On 1 July 1909 in London, Madan Lal Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie and whom else?
x: Dhingra shot Sir William Curzon Wyllie and Cowasji Lalkaka in London on 1 July 1909.

s: Sir William Curzon Wyllie, shot by Madan Lal Dhingra, held which post?
o: Political ADC at the India Office
x: Curzon Wyllie was political ADC at the India Office in London.

s: In which prison was Madan Lal Dhingra hanged in 1909?
x: Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie in London on 1 July 1909 and was hanged at Pentonville Prison, London.

s: Who founded India House (London, 1905)?
x: Shyamji Krishna Varma founded India House; Savarkar, Hardayal and Dhingra worked from it.

s: Who shot Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909?
x: Madan Lal Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie on 1 July 1909; Anant Kanhere killed Jackson at Nasik.

s: For which of the following is Madame Bhikaji Cama known?
o: Leading the Home Rule League in Madras
x: Bhikaji Cama worked for revolutionary nationalism abroad and unfurled an Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907; Congress Radio was Usha Mehta's work.

s: In which year was Curzon Wyllie killed?
x: Curzon Wyllie was killed in 1909, after Khudiram's execution (1908) and before Al-Hilal was started (1912).

s: In which year did Bhikaji Cama unfurl the Indian flag at Stuttgart?
x: Bhikaji Cama unfurled the flag at Stuttgart in 1907, not 1915.

s: The Punjabi edition of *Ghadar* was edited by whom?
x: Kartar Singh Sarabha edited the Punjabi edition of *Ghadar*. *Ghadar di Goonj* consisted of poetry associated with the movement.

s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two publications named Bande Mataram?
o: The Calcutta publication was associated with Bipin Chandra Pal, whereas the publication abroad was associated with Madame Bhikaji Cama.
The Calcutta publication was associated with Shyamji Krishnavarma, whereas the publication abroad was associated with Virendranath Chattopadhyay.
Both were published by Bipin Chandra Pal in Calcutta.
Both were published by Madame Bhikaji Cama in Paris.
x: The Calcutta *Bande Mataram* of 1906 was associated with Bipin Chandra Pal, while Madame Bhikaji Cama brought out *Bande Mataram* abroad.

s: Vanguard was identified as which of the following?
x: Vanguard was an émigré Communist journal run by M.N. Roy from abroad. The Free Press Journal was an English daily and Kesari a Marathi paper.

s: Where did M.N. Roy found the Communist Party of India in 1920?
x: Roy founded the CPI at Tashkent in 1920; the Kanpur formation of 1925 is the date the CPI recognises.

s: Besides the Communist Party of India at Tashkent (1920), the Communist Party of which country is M.N. Roy credited with founding?
x: M.N. Roy founded the Communist Party of Mexico before founding the CPI at Tashkent in 1920. He did not found the communist parties of China, Germany or Indonesia.

s: Who brought out 'Vanguard' (1922), the émigré communist journal?
x: Vanguard (1922) was M.N. Roy's émigré journal, called India's first communist newspaper.

s: The newspaper *Indian Sociologist* was published by Shyamji Krishnavarma from which place?
x: Shyamji Krishnavarma published *Indian Sociologist* from London, in association with India House.

s: Tarak Nath Das published Free Hindustan from which place or region?
x: Tarak Nath Das published Free Hindustan from Vancouver in North America in 1908 to rally Indian emigrants. Allahabad, Patna and Calcutta were home to other papers.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Comrade was Muhammad Ali's paper. Sanjibani was Krishna Kumar Mitra's, Sandhya Brahma Bandhab Upadhyay's and Vande Mataram Pal and Aurobindo's.

s: Who brought out the journal 'Talwar' from Berlin?
x: Talwar (Talvar) was published from Berlin by Virendranath Chattopadhyay.

s: From where did Muhammad Barkatullah publish 'Islamic Fraternity'?
x: Barkatullah brought out Islamic Fraternity from Tokyo.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: *Swadesh Sevak* was associated with G.D. Kumar, not Bipin Chandra Pal. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: With whom was the journal 'Indian Sociologist' associated?
x: Indian Sociologist was associated with Shyamji Krishna Varma abroad; Yugantar and Sandhya were Bengal journals.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Swadesh Sevak was G.D. Kumar's; Bhagwati Charan Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb. Talwar (Chattopadhyay), Islamic Fraternity (Barkatullah) and Indian Sociologist (Shyamji Krishna Varma) are correctly matched.

s: With whom was the journal 'Talwar' associated?
x: Talwar was Virendranath Chattopadhyay's; Islamic Fraternity was Barkatullah's and Swadesh Sevak G.D. Kumar's.

s: Who edited and financed the revolutionary paper 'Bande Mataram' published from Paris in 1909?
x: The Paris Bande Mataram (September 1909) of the Paris Indian Society was edited and financed by Bhikaji Cama.

s: The passengers of the Komagata Maru were denied entry into Canada primarily because of which rule?
x: Canada denied entry under racist immigration laws, particularly the ‘continuous journey’ rule.

s: Which Canadian Prime Minister apologised in the House of Commons in 2016 for the Komagata Maru episode?
x: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau apologised in the Canadian House of Commons in 2016 for the Komagata Maru episode.

s: The Komagata Maru began its voyage to Vancouver from:
x: The ship sailed from Hong Kong via Shanghai, Moji and Yokohama to Vancouver.

s: The police firing at Budge Budge on the returning Komagata Maru passengers took place on:
x: Police fired on the passengers at Budge Budge, near Calcutta, on 29 September 1914.

s: How many Indian passengers did the Komagata Maru carry in 1914?
x: The Komagata Maru carried 376 Indians, mainly Sikhs and Muslims.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Komagata Maru?
o: It was chartered by Baba Gurdit Singh.
It was bound for Vancouver, Canada.
Its passengers were forced back to Bombay.
x: The passengers were forced back to Calcutta, where police fired on them at Budge Budge; the other statements are correct.

s: Who chartered the Komagata Maru?
x: Gurdit Singh, a Punjabi businessman, chartered the Japanese ship Komagata Maru.

s: When did Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
x: Gandhi returned on 9 January 1915, the year Gokhale died; Tilak's League came in April 1916.

s: Into which country were the Komagata Maru passengers (1914) refused entry?
x: The Komagata Maru carried 376 mainly Sikh passengers who were refused entry into Canada and forced back to India.

s: How many passengers were aboard the Komagata Maru (1914)?
x: The Komagata Maru carried 376 mostly Sikh passengers; the Budge Budge firing killed 22.

s: How many people were killed in the Budge Budge firing on the returning Komagata Maru passengers?
x: 22 were killed at Budge Budge when the passengers were forced back to India.

s: Which pair of leaders was associated with the Berlin Committee?
o: Raja Mahendra Pratap and Obaidullah Sindhi
Gurdit Singh and Sohan Singh Bhakna
Shyamji Krishnavarma and Madan Lal Dhingra
x: Virendranath Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta were associated with the Berlin Committee.

s: The revolutionary activities conducted from abroad during the First World War were significant mainly because they:
o: helped internationalise the struggle through arms, funds and foreign support
confined the freedom struggle to constitutional methods within India
restricted revolutionary activities to social reform organisations
ended the activities of Indian revolutionaries outside India
x: Revolutionary networks abroad gave the Indian freedom struggle an international dimension by arranging arms, funds and support from foreign countries during the First World War.

s: After leaving the USA, Lala Har Dayal moved to Switzerland and Germany and joined which body?
x: After his 1914 arrest in the USA, Har Dayal went to Switzerland and Germany and joined the Berlin effort.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the offices in the Provisional Government of India at Kabul?
o: Raja Mahendra Pratap—President; Maulana Barkatullah—Prime Minister
Obaidullah Sindhi—President; Raja Mahendra Pratap—Prime Minister
Raja Mahendra Pratap—Prime Minister; Obaidullah Sindhi—President
x: Raja Mahendra Pratap was President and Maulana Barkatullah was Prime Minister; Obaidullah Sindhi was also associated with the government.

s: The Berlin Committee (1915) sought the help of Germany and ____ to free India.
x: The Berlin Committee sought German and Turkish help to invade India, not French and Russian support.

s: Besides Germany and Turkey, who helped the Provisional Government of India at Kabul?
x: The Kabul government was backed by Germany and Turkey, with help from the Afghan Crown Prince.

s: Who was the Prime Minister of the Provisional Government of India set up at Kabul in 1915?
x: Maulana Barkatullah was Prime Minister; Raja Mahendra Pratap was President.

s: Where was the Provisional Government of India of 1915, with Raja Mahendra Pratap, set up?
x: Raja Mahendra Pratap, Barkatullah and Obaidullah Sindhi were associated with the Provisional Government at Kabul in 1915.

s: With whom was the Berlin Committee (1915) associated?
o: Lala Hardayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
x: The Berlin Committee of Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta sought German and Turkish help.

s: Which Ghadar memoir did Darshi Chenchayya write?
x: Darshi Chenchayya wrote Nenu Naa Desam; Andaman Jeevitam is linked with Prativadi Bhayankaracharyulu.

s: Which one of the following descriptions correctly identifies Darsi Chenchayya?
o: The founder of India House in London
The first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party
The leader of the Komagata Maru voyage
The first Chairman of the Ghadar Party
x: Darsi Chenchayya of Kanigiri is identified as the first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party.

s: What is the title of Darsi Chenchayya's autobiography?
x: Darsi Chenchayya, the only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party, wrote the autobiography Nenu Naa Desam.

s: To which place did Darsi Chenchayya, the only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party, belong?
x: Darsi Chenchayya of Kanigiri was the first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party.

s: Which Ghadar Party leader attended the Palasa Kisan Sabha in Andhra in March 1940?
x: Sohan Singh Bhakna, first president of the Ghadar Party, attended the Palasa Kisan Sabha in March 1940.

s: Which title was given to Annie Besant?
x: Annie Besant was styled the “Iron Lady of Ireland.” She was of Irish origin and later became a prominent Indian nationalist leader.

s: Where was the Central Hindu College founded by Annie Besant in 1898 located?
x: Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College at Varanasi in 1898. It later became the core of Banaras Hindu University under Madan Mohan Malaviya.

s: Which protégé of Annie Besant wrote 'At the Feet of the Master'?
x: Jiddu Krishnamurti, Besant's protégé, wrote At the Feet of the Master.

s: In which year did Annie Besant become President of the Theosophical Society?
x: Besant joined the Theosophical Society in 1889, came to India in 1893 and became its President in 1907.

s: Which bill, drafted by Annie Besant in 1925, proposed dominion status for India?
x: Besant's Commonwealth of India Bill (1925) was a draft dominion constitution with a parliamentary system.

s: Who founded the National College at Madanapalle in 1916?
x: Annie Besant founded the National College, Madanapalle in 1916; its first principal was J.H. Cousins.

s: Who was the first principal of the National College, Madanapalle, founded by Annie Besant in 1916?
x: Besant founded the National College at Madanapalle in 1916; its first principal was J.H. Cousins.

s: In which year did Annie Besant come to India?
x: Besant joined the Theosophical Society in 1889 and came to India in 1893.

s: When did Annie Besant buy the Madras Standard and rename it New India?
x: Annie Besant purchased the Madras Standard in July 1914 and renamed it New India. New India was a daily newspaper.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Vande Matram was an English nationalist paper associated with Aurobindo.
New India was associated with Gandhi and non-violence.
New India was associated with Annie Besant and Home Rule.
x: Option C is incorrect: New India was Annie Besant's Home Rule paper, while Gandhi ran Young India. Tilak's Kesari and Aurobindo's English paper Vande Matram are right.

s: Which INC session did Sarojini Naidu preside over?
x: Sarojini Naidu presided at Kanpur in 1925.

s: After the arrest of which president-elect did Nellie Sengupta become INC President in 1933?
x: Nellie Sengupta presided at Calcutta in 1933 after Malaviya, the president-elect, was arrested.

s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress?
x: Sarojini Naidu (Kanpur, 1925) was the first Indian woman President; Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman President.

s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Tilak's Home Rule League?
o: It was founded by Tilak in 1914 immediately after his release from Mandalay jail.
x: The statement is NOT correct because Tilak's League was founded in April 1916, not in 1914. Tilak was released from Mandalay jail on 16 June 1914.

s: In 1914, Tilak was released from which jail after six years?
x: Tilak was released from Mandalay on 16 June 1914; his League came only in April 1916.

s: During which of the following was the Home Rule Movement launched in India?
x: The Home Rule Leagues were set up in 1916, while the First World War was going on.

s: Where and when was Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League founded?
x: Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League was founded in Madras in September 1916. Its headquarters was at Adyar, in Gokhale Hall.

s: Tilak's Home Rule League operated in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, Berar and which other region?
x: Tilak's League covered Maharashtra except Bombay city, Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar; Besant's covered the rest.

s: Annie Besant's Home Rule League had approximately how many branches?
x: Besant's League covered the rest of India including Bombay city and had about 200 branches.

s: Who was the President of Tilak's Home Rule League?
x: Joseph Baptista was President and N.C. Kelkar Secretary of Tilak's League; Arundale and Wadia were with Besant's League.

s: Into which body did Tilak's Home Rule League finally merge?
o: Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League
x: Tilak's League merged into Besant's All India Home Rule League, which in 1920 became the Swarajya Sabha under Gandhi and merged into the Congress.

s: Where was the headquarters of Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League?
x: Besant's League was based at Adyar (Gokhale Hall), Madras; Tilak's was based at Poona.

s: Where was the Bombay Provincial Conference held at which Tilak's Home Rule League was founded on 28 April 1916?
x: It was launched at Belgaum; the League was then based at Poona.

s: Who was the Secretary of Tilak's Home Rule League?
x: N.C. Kelkar was Secretary and Joseph Baptista President of Tilak's League; Arundale and Wadia were with Besant's.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League?
o: Its headquarters was at Adyar, Madras.
Its area of work excluded Bombay city.
x: Besant's League covered the rest of India including Bombay city; it was Tilak's League that excluded Bombay city.

s: Under whose presidency was the All India Home Rule League renamed Swarajya Sabha in 1920?
x: In 1920 the All India Home Rule League, with Gandhi as President, was renamed Swarajya Sabha and soon merged into the Congress.

s: Who was the organising secretary of Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League?
x: George Arundale was organising secretary of Besant's League; Baptista and Kelkar held posts in Tilak's League.

s: Who popularised the Home Rule Movement in the United Provinces?
x: Jinnah carried the Home Rule Movement to UP.

s: Who was the General Secretary of the Madras Home Rule League?
x: In the Madras League, C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar was General Secretary and B.P. Wadia was Treasurer.

s: Which of the following came first?
x: Tilak's League came in April 1916, Besant's in September 1916, the Lucknow Pact in December 1916 and the Montagu Declaration in August 1917.

s:
Consider the following statements about the chronology of the period:
1. The Komagata Maru incident preceded Gandhi's return from South Africa.
2. Besant's Home Rule League was founded before Tilak's.
3. The Montagu Declaration came after the Lucknow Pact.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Komagata Maru (1914) preceded Gandhi's return (January 1915), and the Montagu Declaration (August 1917) followed the Lucknow Pact (December 1916). Tilak's League (April 1916) came before Besant's (September 1916).

s: When was Tilak's Home Rule League started?
x: Tilak's Home Rule League began in April 1916, Besant's in September 1916.

s: When did Annie Besant start her Home Rule League?
x: Tilak's Home Rule League began in April 1916 and Annie Besant's in September 1916.

s: Which popular title of Tilak means 'beloved of the people'?
x: Lokmanya was Tilak's popular title; 'Father of Indian Unrest' came from Valentine Chirol.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Tilak's newspapers is correctly matched?
x: Tilak founded or edited Kesari as a Marathi paper and Mahratta as an English paper; both are associated with the year 1881.

s: Which one of the following pairs of quotation and leader is NOT correctly matched?
o: Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it" — B.G. Tilak
First we are Indians, then only Muslims" — M.A. Jinnah
Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers" — Annie Besant
Shiva cut his wife into fifty-two pieces..." — Edwin Montagu
x: "Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers" was Tilak's remark on the Lucknow Pact, not Besant's. The Swaraj slogan was Tilak's, the 'first we are Indians' line Jinnah's, and the Shiva remark Montagu's on Besant's internment.

s: Who said of the Lucknow Pact, "Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"?
x: Tilak, not Besant, made this remark on the Lucknow Pact.

s: Who gave the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"?
x: The slogan is Bal Gangadhar Tilak's.

s: Who said, "The British Empire is rotten to the core, corrupt in every direction"?
x: This remark on the British Empire was made by Sister Nivedita.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Quote)
a. Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
b. I am an Indian Tom-Tom
c. The British Empire is rotten to the core
d. First we are Indians, then only Muslims
List-II (Leader)
1. Sister Nivedita
2. M.A. Jinnah
3. Bal Gangadhar Tilak
4. Annie Besant
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Swaraj birthright = Tilak; Indian Tom-Tom = Besant; rotten to the core = Sister Nivedita; First we are Indians = Jinnah.

s: Where was the Surat split of 1907 between the Moderates and Extremists healed?
x: The split that occurred at Surat in 1907 was healed at the Lucknow session in 1916.

s: The reunion of the Moderates and Extremists at Lucknow was facilitated mainly by:
o: The formation of the Indian National Liberal Federation alone
Tilak and Besant's efforts, along with the deaths of Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta
x: Tilak and Besant worked for reunion, while the deaths of Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta in 1915 removed important obstacles to reconciliation.

s: Who were the main negotiators of the Lucknow Pact of 1916?
x: Tilak and Jinnah were the key negotiators of the Lucknow Pact.

s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 is significant in the history of communal politics because the Congress:
o: Rejected all forms of communal representation
x: Through the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.

s: In which year did the Surat Split take place?
x: The Surat Split between Moderates and Extremists happened in 1907 and was healed at Lucknow in 1916.

s: Who led the Home Rule Movement?
o: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant
Lala Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo Ghosh
x: The Home Rule Movement was led by Tilak and Annie Besant; Das and Motilal Nehru led the Swaraj Party.

s: Which one of the following best explains the historical significance of the Home Rule Movement?
o: It restricted nationalist activity to the major presidency towns.
It replaced the Congress permanently with the Muslim League.
It ended all political work until the Non-Cooperation Movement.
It filled the gap between Gokhale's death and Gandhi's rise, while preparing cadres and organisations for later mass politics.
x: The movement bridged the period between Gokhale's death in 1915 and Gandhi's rise in 1920, built countryside organisation and trained cadres who later participated in Gandhian movements.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Leader is linked with Madan Mohan Malviya. The Bombay Chronicle was Pherozeshah Mehta's, Justice T.M. Nair's and Searchlight Sachidanand Sinha's.

s: Who made the remark about Shiva cutting his wife into fifty-two pieces, in the context of Annie Besant's internment?
x: Edwin Montagu used the remark while commenting on the folly of Annie Besant's internment.

s: Annie Besant was interned on 15 June 1917 at which place along with B. P. Wadia and G. S. Arundale?
x: Annie Besant was interned at Ootacamund on 15 June 1917 along with B. P. Wadia and G. S. Arundale.

s: What was the effect of Annie Besant's internment on the Home Rule Movement?
x: Besant's internment aroused public outrage, strengthened the movement and drew several Moderates into it.

s: The central objective expressed in the Montagu Declaration was:
o: Immediate complete independence from British rule
Progressive realisation of responsible government through self-governing institutions
Introduction of separate electorates for all communities
x: The Declaration promised the gradual development of self-governing institutions and the progressive realisation of responsible government by increasing Indian participation in administration.

s: The Congress special session at Bombay (August 1918), which split over the Mont-Ford proposals, was presided over by:
x: Hasan Imam presided over the Bombay special session of August 1918.

s: When was Annie Besant released from internment?
x: Besant, interned on 15 June 1917, was released on 17 September 1917 under Congress-League pressure.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the August Declaration?
o: It promised the progressive realisation of responsible government.
It was announced by Edwin Montagu as Viceroy of India.
It led on to the Act of 1919.
x: Montagu was Secretary of State; the Viceroy was Lord Chelmsford. The other statements are correct.

s: Who announced the August Declaration of 20 August 1917?
x: It was announced by Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State; Chelmsford was the Viceroy.

s: What sentence did Batukeshwar Dutt receive in the Central Assembly bomb case?
x: B.K. Dutt was given transportation for life; he was not hanged.

s: Which of the following was sentenced to transportation for life, not hanged, in the Lahore Conspiracy Case?
x: Kishori Lal got transportation for life; Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929-31)?
o: It was tried by a special tribunal set up by the Governor-General.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931.
Shiv Verma was sentenced to transportation for life.
The death sentence was pronounced in October 1929.
x: The death sentence was pronounced in October 1930, not 1929; the other statements are correct.

s: To which movement did the first Lahore Conspiracy Case (1915) relate?
x: The 1915 case was the Ghadar case; Bhagat Singh's (1929-31) was the second.

s: Jatin Das died in Lahore jail after a hunger strike of how many days?
x: Jatin Das died after 63 days of hunger strike in September 1929.

s: On which date were Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru executed after the Lahore Conspiracy Case?
x: The Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929-30) ended with their execution on 23 March 1931.

s: Jatin Das died after how many days of hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929?
x: Jatin Das died after 63 days of hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929 and was regarded as the first martyr of that strike.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the HRA and HSRA?
o: The HRA was founded at Kanpur in 1924
Bhagat Singh reorganised the organisation after Bismil's death
The HSRA stood for socialist revolution
Bhagat Singh is credited with founding the HSRA
x: It was Chandrashekhar Azad who reorganised the organisation after Bismil's death.

s: The HSRA aimed to set up which of the following?
o: Federal Republic of United States of India
x: The HSRA envisaged a 'Federal Republic of United States of India' and advocated socialist revolution.

s: The HSRA added ____ to the HRA's objective of establishing a republic through armed revolt.
x: The HSRA added socialism to the HRA's aim, an ideological development beyond the HRA.

s: Which of the following was a mass-propaganda method of the HSRA-era revolutionaries?
o: Exclusive reliance on secret military training
x: Courtroom proceedings, leaflets and hunger strikes were used as mass propaganda.

s: Where was the Hindustan Republican Association founded in October 1924?
x: The HRA was founded at Kanpur in October 1924; the HSRA at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, in 1928.

s: Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad reorganised the HRA in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla, Delhi, into which organisation?
x: In 1928 the HRA was renamed the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) under Bhagat Singh and Azad. Anushilan Samiti was Bengali, Abhinav Bharat was Savarkar's and Khudai Khidmatgar was Ghaffar Khan's.

s: Who among the following was a founder of the Hindustan Republican Association in 1924?
x: The HRA was founded at Kanpur in 1924 by Ram Prasad Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee and Sachindra Nath Sanyal.

s: Who founded the Indian Republican Army of Chittagong?
x: The Indian Republican Army was Surya Sen's group at Chittagong.

s: Who founded the Khudai Khidmatgar?
x: The Khudai Khidmatgar was founded by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

s: With whom is the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army in Madras (1933) associated?
x: Kanuru Ramanatha Choudary is linked with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army, Madras, 10 March 1933.

s: After the death of Ram Prasad Bismil, into which body did Chandrashekhar Azad reorganise the Hindustan Republican Association?
x: Chandrashekhar Azad reorganised the Hindustan Republican Association into the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association after Bismil’s death.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Hindustan Republican Association was founded in Kanpur in 1924. HSRA was formed in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Naujawan Bharat Sabha in Lahore in 1926, and the Indian Independence League in 1942.

s: Where was the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association formed in 1928?
x: Chandrashekhar Azad, with Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev, formed the HSRA at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, in 1928.

s: The Hindustan Republican Association was formed after which event?
o: The suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement
x: The HRA (Kanpur, 1924) was formed by young men disappointed by the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

s: In which year was the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) formed?
x: The HSRA was formed in 1928, after the HRA (1924) and the Kakori action (1925).

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Kakori train action
2. Hindustan Republican Association
3. Hindustan Socialist Republican Association
4. Naujawan Bharat Sabha
x: HRA 1924, Kakori 1925, Naujawan Bharat Sabha 1926, HSRA 1928.

s: For whom was J.P. Saunders mistaken when he was killed at Lahore in 1928?
x: Saunders was mistakenly killed in place of James A. Scott, associated with the anti-Simon lathi-charge.

s: On which date did Udham Singh shoot Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London?
x: Udham Singh shot O'Dwyer on 13 March 1940 in revenge for Jallianwala Bagh.

s: Whom did Gopinath Saha shoot by mistake while trying to kill Charles Tegart in 1924?
x: Gopinath Saha shot Ernest Day by mistake on 12 January 1924 in Calcutta.

s: Udham Singh killed Michael O'Dwyer in 1940 to avenge which event?
x: O'Dwyer was Punjab's Lt. Governor at the time of Jallianwala Bagh; Udham Singh killed him in revenge.

s: Who fired the first shot at J.P. Saunders in Lahore in December 1928?
x: Rajguru fired first, then Bhagat Singh; Azad covered the retreat.

s: The Central Assembly bomb incident was primarily a protest against which Bills?
o: The Government of India Bill and the Rowlatt Bill
The Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill
The Trade Disputes Bill and the Indian Councils Bill
The Rowlatt Bill and the Public Safety Bill
x: The action protested against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill, which were viewed as curbing civil liberties and workers' rights.

s: The leaflet thrown in the Central Assembly in 1929 said the action was 'to make the ____ hear'.
x: The leaflet said 'To make the deaf hear'; Bhagat Singh and Dutt then courted arrest to use the court as a platform.

s: Who wrote the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'?
x: Maulana Hasrat Mohani wrote 'Inquilab Zindabad'; Bhagat Singh made it popular.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Assembly bomb incident (1929):
1. Non-lethal smoke bombs were thrown.
2. It protested against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.
3. Batukeshwar Dutt was hanged for it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Smoke bombs were thrown to protest the Public Safety and Trade Disputes Bills. B.K. Dutt got transportation for life and was not hanged.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Batukeshwar Dutt – Central Legislative Assembly bombing
Ram Prasad Bismil – Chittagong Armoury Raid
x: Batukeshwar Dutt carried out the Central Assembly bombing with Bhagat Singh. Bismil led Kakori for the HRA, Surya Sen the Chittagong raid, and Savarkar founded Abhinav Bharat.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Assembly bomb of 8 April 1929?
o: It protested against the Public Safety Bill
It protested against the Trade Disputes Bill
The bombs were meant to kill members of the Assembly
The bombs were thrown by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt
x: The bombs were deliberately non-lethal, 'to make the deaf hear', aiming at arrest and a trial for propaganda.

s: The Saunders killing of 1928 was meant to avenge the lathi-charge on whom?
x: The Saunders killing was planned in retaliation for the lathi-charge on Lala Lajpat Rai during the anti-Simon Commission protest. The intended target was James A. Scott, while Rajguru fired first.

s: Who was the intended target in the Saunders killing of 1928?
x: The revolutionaries aimed at James A. Scott to avenge the lathi-charge on Lajpat Rai; Saunders was killed instead.

s: Which one of the following sets contains only those executed in connection with the Kakori Train Action?
o: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri
Surya Sen, Ananta Singh, Ganesh Ghosh and Lokenath Bal
Jatin Das, Chandrashekhar Azad, Udham Singh and Gopinath Saha
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru and Batukeshwar Dutt
x: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged in connection with the Kakori case in December 1927.

s: The Kakori Train Action was undertaken primarily to:
o: protest against the Trade Disputes Bill
destroy the railway line between Delhi and Lahore
obtain government treasury funds for the HRA
x: On 9 August 1925, the HRA looted the government treasury carried on a train near Kakori to fund its revolutionary activities.

s: In which jail was Ashfaqullah Khan hanged in the Kakori case?
x: Ashfaqullah Khan was hanged at Faizabad; Bismil at Gorakhpur, Lahiri at Gonda, Roshan Singh at Naini.

s: Which of the following pairs of Kakori revolutionary and place of hanging is correctly matched?
x: Rajendra Lahiri was hanged at Gonda; Bismil at Gorakhpur, Ashfaqullah at Faizabad and Roshan Singh at Naini.

s: How many persons were arrested in the Kakori case?
x: 43 people were arrested; four of them were hanged in December 1927.

s: Near which city did the Kakori train action of 9 August 1925 take place?
x: The HRA looted the government treasury on a train at Kakori near Lucknow, on the Lucknow-Saharanpur section.

s: Who among the following was hanged in the Kakori case?
x: Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged for Kakori; Jogesh Chatterjee got life and Azad escaped.

s: Where was the Naujawan Bharat Sabha, founded by Bhagat Singh in 1926, set up?
x: It was founded at Lahore in 1926 with Sukhdev and Bhagwati Charan Vohra; Delhi 1928 (Feroz Shah Kotla) is the HSRA.

s: What was the principal objective of the Naujawan Bharat Sabha?
o: mobilise youth, peasants and workers and oppose communalism
establish a princely federation through constitutional reforms
secure separate electorates for revolutionary organisations
organise military assistance for the British during the First World War
x: The Sabha sought to mobilise youth, peasants and workers and to fight communalism.

s: Who among the following helped Bhagat Singh found the Naujawan Bharat Sabha in 1926?
x: Bhagat Singh founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha at Lahore in 1926 with Sukhdev and Bhagwati Charan Vohra.

s: In which year did the Nankana Sahib incident, which influenced Bhagat Singh, take place?
x: Jallianwala Bagh (1919), Nankana Sahib (1921) and Chauri Chaura (1922) preceded Bhagat Singh's turn to revolutionary politics.

s: Who wrote the poem 'Sarfaroshi Ki Tamanna Ab Hamare Dil Mein Hai'?
x: The poem was written by Bismil Azimabadi; Ram Prasad Bismil made it famous.

s: Who wrote *The Philosophy of the Bomb* as a reply to Gandhi's *The Cult of the Bomb*?
x: *The Philosophy of the Bomb* was written by Bhagwati Charan Vohra as a reply to Gandhi's *The Cult of the Bomb*.

s: Who wrote 'An Introduction to the Dreamland'?
x: Bhagat Singh wrote An Introduction to the Dreamland.

s: Which book was written by Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee?
x: Jogesh Chatterjee wrote In Search of Freedom; Bandi Jiwan was by Sachindranath Sanyal.

s: Who wrote 'Why I am an Atheist'?
x: Bhagat Singh wrote Why I am an Atheist; Bhagwati Charan Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb.

s: Where did the fighting associated with the Chittagong Armoury Raid take place?
x: The raiders cut telegraph lines, disrupted railways and fought at the Jalalabad Hills.

s: In which year was Surya Sen, leader of the Chittagong Armoury Raid, hanged?
x: Surya Sen, whose group called itself the Indian Republican Army, was hanged in 1934; the 1931 Lahore executions were of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bina Das — fired at the Bengal Governor at a convocation
Pritilata Waddedar — Pahartali European Club raid
Kalpana Dutt — sentenced to life imprisonment
Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury — led the Pahartali European Club raid
x: Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury shot the District Magistrate at Comilla. The Pahartali European Club raid was led by Pritilata Waddedar, who took cyanide.

s: Which raid did Pritilata Waddedar lead?
x: Pritilata Waddedar led the raid on the Pahartali European Club and took cyanide.

s: Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury shot the District Magistrate of which place?
x: In December 1931 Santi Ghosh and Suniti Choudhury shot the District Magistrate at Comilla.

s:
Consider the following statements about the women of the Chittagong movement:
1. Pritilata Waddedar took cyanide.
2. Kalpana Dutt was hanged.
3. Bina Das fired at the Bengal Governor at her convocation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Pritilata took cyanide and Bina Das fired at the Governor in February 1932. Kalpana Dutt was sentenced to life, not hanged.

s: Who among the following was an associate of Surya Sen in the Chittagong Armoury Raid?
x: Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh and Ambika Chakravarty were Surya Sen's associates in the raid.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Chittagong Armoury Raid took place in April 1930, not 1929; the other pairs are correct.

s: In which year did the Chittagong Armoury Raid take place?
x: The Chittagong Armoury Raid was in 1930.

s: Who led the Chittagong Armoury Raid of 1930?
x: Surya Sen ('Masterda') led the Chittagong Armoury Raid of April 1930.

s: Where did Chandrashekhar Azad shoot himself on 27 February 1931?
x: Azad shot himself at Alfred Park, Prayagraj, on 27 February 1931. Feroz Shah Kotla was where the HSRA was formed in 1928; Kakori was the 1925 train action; Lahore jail was the scene of Jatin Das's hunger strike and the 1931 executions.

s:
Consider the following statements about birth years of revolutionaries:
1. Bhagat Singh was born in 1907.
2. Chandrashekhar Azad was born in 1906.
3. Khudiram Bose was born in 1889.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All are correct: Bhagat Singh 28 Sep 1907, Azad 23 Jul 1906, Khudiram 3 Dec 1889.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ram Prasad Bismil was born on 11 June 1897.
2. Sukhdev was born at Ludhiana in 1907.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Bismil was born on 11 June 1897 and Sukhdev on 15 May 1907 at Ludhiana.

s: Where did Chandrashekhar Azad shoot himself during a police encounter?
x: Azad shot himself at Alfred Park after resisting capture; he was not executed in the Kakori or Lahore cases.

s: When was Bhagat Singh born?
x: Bhagat Singh was born on 28 September 1907; 23 July 1906 is Azad's and 15 May 1907 Sukhdev's birth date.

s: Where was Rajguru (Shivaram Hari) born in 1908?
x: Rajguru was born at Khed, now Rajgurunagar, Maharashtra.

s: On which date did Chandrashekhar Azad die at Alfred Park?
x: Azad shot himself in a police encounter at Alfred Park on 27 February 1931.

s: Where was Chandrashekhar Azad born in 1906?
x: Azad was born on 23 July 1906 at Bhavra in Madhya Pradesh.

s: At which institution did Sukhdev teach?
x: Sukhdev taught at the National College, Lahore.

s: Which lieutenant of Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 June 1924?
x: Gam Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924; Gam Mallu Dora was arrested in 1923 and later became an MP in 1952.

s: Which associate of Alluri Sitarama Raju later became an MP in 1952?
x: Gam Mallu Dora, Raju's 'right hand', was arrested in 1923, given a life term and became an MP in 1952; Gantam Dora was killed in 1924.

s: In whose presence was Alluri Sitarama Raju shot at Koyyuru in 1924?
x: Raju was captured by Jamadar Kanchu Meenan and shot at Koyyuru before Major Goodall on 7 May 1924.

s: Who captured Alluri Sitarama Raju before he was shot at Koyyuru in 1924?
x: Alluri was captured by Jamadar Kanchu Meenan and shot at Koyyuru before Major Goodall on 7 May 1924.

s: The Rampa or Manyam Rebellion was principally based in which area?
o: The Gudem hills of the East Godavari Agency
x: The rebellion was based in the Gudem hills, located in the Agency area of East Godavari.

s: In which area did the Rampa Rebellion, an armed tribal rebellion, take place?
x: It was an armed tribal rebellion in the Agency area, not affiliated with the Congress, and troubled the British more than the Non-Cooperation Movement.

s: Where did Alluri Sitarama Raju's forces suffer their first defeat at the hands of the Malabar Special Police?
x: At Peddagaddapalem on 6 December 1922, the Malabar Special Police inflicted Raju’s first defeat; he was wounded at Lingapuram.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 24 September 1922 — officers Scott Coward and Heiter killed at Damanapalli ghat
6 December 1922 — Gam Mallu Dora arrested at Nadimpalem
7 May 1924 — Gam Gantam Dora killed in firing
x: Scott Coward and Heiter were killed at Damanapalli ghat on 24 September 1922. Mallu Dora was arrested in September 1923, Raju was shot on 7 May 1924, and Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924.

s: Which British officer was appointed Special Commissioner to crush the Rampa rebellion?
x: Rutherford served as Special Commissioner to crush the revolt and ordered the exile of 55 helpers; warrants were issued for 183 persons.

s: Which British officers were killed at Damanapalli ghat on 24 Sept 1922?
x: Scott Coward and Heiter were killed at Damanapalli ghat on 24 Sept 1922.

s: Who was the officer who arrested Gam Mallu Dora?
x: Keirns arrested Gam Mallu Dora in 1923.

s: During which period did the Rampa rebellion take place?
x: The Rampa rebellion ran from August 1922 to May 1924, about 1 year 9 months. It began with the attack on Chintapalli police station on 22 August 1922, and Raju was shot at Koyyuru on 7 May 1924.

s: Why did Alluri Sitarama Raju's rebels raid police stations such as Chintapalli and Rajavommangi?
o: To seize British arms and use them against the British
x: The Rampa rebels raided police stations to seize British arms and then used those arms against the British.

s:
Match the following:
List-I
A. Chintapalli
B. Peddagaddapalem
C. Koyyuru
D. Krishnadevipeta
List-II
1. Samadhi of Alluri Sitarama Raju
2. Alluri shot dead
3. First defeat of Raju's forces
4. First police station attacked
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Chintapalli was the first station attacked (22 Aug 1922), Peddagaddapalem the first defeat (6 Dec 1922), Koyyuru where Raju was shot (7 May 1924) and Krishnadevipeta where his samadhi stands.

s: Who were the lieutenants associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju during the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora
x: Gam Mallu Dora and Gam Gantam Dora were associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju as lieutenants. Scott Coward and Haytes were officers killed during the rebellion.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Rampa Rebellion is NOT correct?
o: Scott Coward and Haytes were killed during the rebellion.
The Malabar Special Police was brought in against the rebels.
Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 May 1922.
A direct battle took place at Panjerighat.
x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 May 1924, not 1922. The other three statements are correct.

s: Alluri Sitarama Raju's armed struggle is said to have troubled the British more than which movement?
x: Raju was not linked to the INC, but his armed struggle troubled the British more than the Non-Cooperation Movement.

s: When was Alluri Sitarama Raju killed?
x: Raju was killed on 7 May 1924, not 1922; 22 August 1922 was his first attack, on Chintapalli.

s: Which police station did Alluri Sitarama Raju attack first, on 22 August 1922?
x: The Rampa Rebellion began with the raid on Chintapalli police station on 22 August 1922; Krishnadevipeta and Rajavommangi followed.

s: Which police station was attacked first during the Rampa Rebellion?
x: The Rampa Rebellion began on August 22, 1922, when Alluri Sitarama Raju's men raided the Chintapalli police station. Kanikapadu and Nidubrolu are linked with N.G. Ranga.

s: On which date did the Rampa Rebellion led by Alluri Sitarama Raju begin?
x: The Rampa Rebellion began on 22 August 1922 with a raid on Chintapalli police station.

s: Which tribes mainly took part in the Rampa Rebellion (1922-24) led by Alluri Sitarama Raju?
x: The Rampa Rebellion in the Godavari agency was fought by Koyas and Konda Doras.

s: Which police station was attacked first by Alluri Sitarama Raju?
x: Alluri Sitarama Raju began the Rampa revolt of 1922 by attacking the Chintapalli police station first. Palnadu is linked with the Forest Satyagraha and Kakinada with the Vandemataram riot case.

s: Where was the AICC meeting of 1921 held that helped bring Gandhi's programme into Andhra?
x: The Bezawada AICC meeting of 1921 helped put Gandhi's programme into Andhra.

s: Which period is called the 'Glorious Decade' of Andhra?
x: 1921-31 is called the 'Glorious Decade' of Andhra.

s: Which AICC meeting of 5 Nov 1921 allowed provincial committees to start civil disobedience, including no-tax?
x: The Delhi AICC of 5 Nov 1921 let provincial committees start civil disobedience including no-tax, which Guntur took up.

s:
Match the following:
List-I
A. Chirala-Perala movement
B. Palnadu pullari movement
C. Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign
D. Rampa rebellion
List-II
1. Alluri Sitarama Raju
2. Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary
3. Kanneganti Hanumanthu
4. Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Chirala-Perala was led by Duggirala, Palnadu by Kanneganti Hanumanthu, Pedanandipadu by Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary and the Rampa rebellion by Alluri.

s: Which Congress leader urged restraint during the Pedanandipadu campaign?
x: Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri backed the campaign, whereas Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint.

s: During the Pedanandipadu campaign, Rutherford's proposal to ban which body was rejected by the Madras Government?
x: Rutherford was deployed to deal with the campaign, but his proposal to ban the Shanti Sena was rejected.

s: At which village was Kanneganti Hanumanthu killed in police firing during the Palnadu pullari movement?
x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed in police firing at Minchalapadu during the Palnadu pullari movement.

s: On which date was the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign suspended after the Guntur District Congress Committee received Gandhi's message to Konda Venkatappayya?
x: Gandhi’s message to suspend the campaign reached the Guntur District Congress Committee on 11 February 1922, after which the campaign ended with the Non-Cooperation Movement.

s: How many of the 19 village officers of the Pedanandipadu firka resigned during the 1922 no-tax campaign?
x: 18 of the 19 village officers in the firka resigned during the campaign.

s: The Palnadu movement of 1921-22 refused which tax?
x: Palnadu refused pullari, the grazing (grass) tax on forest land; Pedanandipadu refused land revenue.

s: Which tax did the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign of 1922 refuse to pay?
x: Pedanandipadu refused land revenue, when the first instalment fell due in January-February 1922.

s: What was the name of the volunteer force of Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary in the Pedanandipadu campaign?
x: Shanti Sena belonged to Parvataneni (Pedanandipadu); Ramadandu was Duggirala's corps at Chirala-Perala.

s: Which Revenue Board member blamed the Congress and was sent to Guntur during the no-tax campaign?
x: Revenue Board member L.T. Harris blamed the Congress and was sent to Guntur; Rutherford's plan to ban the Shanti Sena was rejected.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign:
1. The Shanti Sena was decided upon by the Guntur DCC in Dec 1921.
2. The campaign was suspended on 11 Feb 1922 after Gandhi's message to Konda Venkatappayya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the Guntur DCC decided on the Shanti Sena in Dec 1921, and the campaign was suspended on 11 Feb 1922.

s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led which movement in Guntur district?
x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu pullari (grazing tax) movement of 1921-22 and was killed in police firing at Minchalapadu.

s: In which year did the Palnadu pullari (grass tax) movement begin?
x: The Palnadu pullari movement ran in 1921-22, during the Non-Cooperation Movement.

s: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary is remembered as the leader of which movement?
x: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary ('Andhra Shivaji') led the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign of Jan-Feb 1922 with his Shanti Sena.

s: Who among the following was a member of the Congress committee that inquired into the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign?
x: T. Prakasam, Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao and Dantu Narayana Raju formed the inquiry committee; it praised the campaign and advised waiting for Bardoli.

s: Who led the resignation of village officers in the Pedanandipadu firka in 1922?
x: Chandavolu karanam Machiraju Ramamurthy led the resignations; 18 of the 19 village officers of the firka resigned.

s: Which leader backed Kanneganti Hanumanthu in the Palnadu pullari movement?
x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu pullari movement with the backing of Unnava Lakshminarayana.

s: Chirala, Perala and Pedanandipadu all lay in which taluka of Guntur district?
x: Chirala, Perala and Pedanandipadu were all in Bapatla taluka of Guntur district.

s: Minchalapadu, where Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed, lies in which area of Guntur district?
x: Minchalapadu is a Palnadu village of Guntur district, scene of the pullari movement.

s: Who founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala?
x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala.

s: Who introduced Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya to Gandhi in London in 1915?
x: Ananda K. Coomaraswamy introduced Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya to Gandhi in London in 1915 and described him as the coming man of his country.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma — Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi
x: B is correct: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led the Chirala-Perala movement (1921). A is wrong: the Ramadandu was Duggirala's volunteer corps, not Alluri's; C is wrong: Pisapati Narayana Sastri wrote Chirala Perala Vanavasam; D is wrong: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was the first woman jailed at Chirala-Perala, while Duggirala founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi.

s: Why did the Chirala-Perala Satyagraha arise?
o: The British prohibited the Ramadandu from holding public meetings.
The villages were brought under the Forest Act and denied podu rights.
The two villages were converted into a municipality and their annual tax burden increased sharply.
The residents were forced to migrate to the Gudem hills.
x: Chirala and Perala were made a municipality, and the annual tax rose from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000, provoking the movement.

s: What was the name of the camp set up outside municipal limits by the residents during the Chirala-Perala movement?
x: The residents set up Ramnagar (Ramanagaram) with a parallel all-caste assembly and arbitration court; it lasted about 11 months.

s: Why was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya arrested on 1 October 1921?
o: Broke a ban on public speaking after his Berhampur speech
Organised an armed raid in the Gudem hills
Refused to pay the municipal tax
x: After his Berhampur speech, Duggirala was prohibited from speaking for two months. He defied the ban and was arrested on 1 October 1921.

s: During which ministry was the municipality of Chirala and Perala abolished in 1938?
o: Rajagopalachari, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
Tanguturi Prakasam, with Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya as minister concerned
P. Subbarayan, with Konda Venkatappayya as minister concerned
Bobbili Raja, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
x: The municipality was abolished in 1938 during the Rajaji ministry, when Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the Local Self-Government Minister.

s: Who is the author of the book 'Chirala Perala Vanavasam'?
x: *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by Pisapati Narayana Sastri.

s: From which university did Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya take his M.A. (Hons) in Economics in 1916?
x: Duggirala took an M.A. (Hons) in Economics from the University of Edinburgh in 1916 and was Secretary of the Edinburgh Indian Association.

s: After the Non-Cooperation Movement, Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya joined which party as an Andhra secretary?
x: After the NCM he joined the Swaraj Party of C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru as an Andhra secretary.

s: By how much did the yearly tax rise when Chirala and Perala were made a municipality?
x: Making Chirala-Perala a municipality (Jan 1920) raised the yearly tax from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000.

s: Who was the first woman jailed in the Chirala-Perala movement?
x: Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma was the first woman jailed; Duvvuri Subbamma was also arrested but was not the first.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Chirala-Perala movement:
1. On 25 April 1921, 13,572 of 15,326 residents left the town.
2. The Ramnagar camp with its parallel self-rule lasted about 11 months.
3. Duggirala was tried by Rutherford at Srikakulam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
